output.brief:
The stops come from two things together: firmware 6.4 and the new gloss pallet wrap. Neither causes them alone.

Version 6.4 keeps weak short-range returns that 6.3 threw away. At shallow angles the gloss film produces exactly those returns, so the robots treat staged pallets as obstacles.

Three pieces of evidence point this way:
- In a bench test with no people present, 6.4 on gloss film stopped 17 times in 20 passes. 6.3 on gloss stopped once. 6.4 on the old matte film stopped 0 times.
- Pallet robots on 6.4 in Zones A and B went from 3.2 to 15.6 stops per 100 hours. The eight robots left on 6.3 in the same zones stayed at about 3.
- Tote robots on 6.4 in Zone C, where no wrapped pallets are staged, did not change.

The temps are not the driver. Don't introduce the three-strike policy, and don't shorten the protective fields.

Missed cut-offs rose with peak volume in 2025 too, while stops stayed flat. The stops may add to the misses, but that is not shown.

Next steps:
1. Switch outbound pallets back to the matte film.
2. Track stops weekly by zone and firmware group.
3. If stops don't fall, roll the 30 upgraded pallet robots back to 6.3 under a waiver. Security support for 6.3 ends 31 October.
4. Don't treat the December release as the fix until it has been tested on this film.

I'm fairly confident in this, though it rests on one bench test and one site analysis.
